headline: Software Leads a Fractured Monday as Chips Sink and Staffing Shines
body_html:
Monday's session closed on a split note, with the dominant story being a sharp divergence between software's resurgence and a bruising retreat in semiconductors. Of the 501 names tracked, 324 finished higher against 176 decliners — a reasonably healthy breadth reading that masked the brutality at the sector extremes. Software surged 3.38%, anchored by strong individual moves from supply-chain and design names, while Semiconductors shed 2.15% and Energy gave back 1.92%, the latter dragged lower as crude futures slid on a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities that cooled the geopolitical risk premium.

The rotation was unmistakable: money that exited chip stocks and energy found a home in Consumer names, up 2.27%, and Healthcare, which added 1.38%. Homebuilders edged 0.99% higher, a quiet beneficiary of falling yields that accompanied oil's drop. Industrials and Materials were near-flat, suggesting the rotation was targeted rather than broad cyclical enthusiasm.

The session's standout mover was Robert Half, the staffing specialist, which surged 12.04% — a sharp reminder that in a mixed tape, earnings catalysts can cut through the noise entirely. With the Federal Reserve's decision looming later in the week, Monday felt less like a directional bet and more like a market repositioning for what comes next.

briefs.headline: Crude Falls as U.S.-Iran Standoff Enters a Pause
briefs.body: Oil futures declined sharply Monday after reports emerged that the United States and Iran had temporarily halted direct hostilities, draining the geopolitical premium that had supported crude prices. The retreat weighed on Energy sector names across the board, which collectively shed 1.92%. Gold, by contrast, gained more than 1% as investors sought a less correlated safe-haven with the Fed meeting on deck.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Complex Takes the Session's Heaviest Blow
briefs.body: Memory and analog chip names led the market lower on Monday, with Sandisk tumbling 12.22%, MaxLinear off nearly 11%, and semiconductor-equipment supplier Ichor Holdings dropping 10.79%. The sector as a whole fell 2.15%, extending a stretch of pressure on chip stocks as investors weighed demand signals and the broader implications of large capital commitments circulating in the AI ecosystem.

briefs.headline: Manhattan Associates Rockets on Supply-Chain Strength
briefs.body: Supply-chain software specialist Manhattan Associates climbed 9.64% to rank among Monday's top performers, reinforcing Software's position as the session's leading sector with a 3.38% gain. Autodesk added 7.71% in the design-software space, and N-able rose 8.70%, suggesting broad-based appetite for enterprise and cloud-adjacent software names as investors rotated away from hardware.

briefs.headline: Abercrombie Leads Consumer Apparel Higher
briefs.body: Abercrombie & Fitch jumped 9.27% on Monday, helping lift the broader Consumer sector to a 2.27% gain and signaling continued resilience in discretionary spending. The move suggested investors are not yet pricing in a significant deterioration in the U.S. consumer, even as macro uncertainties persist heading into the Federal Reserve's mid-week policy announcement.

briefs.headline: Fed Chair Warsh's Tone in Focus as Rate Decision Nears
briefs.body: Prediction markets on Kalshi were actively pricing scenarios around Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's language at this week's policy meeting, with traders parsing whether his remarks will lean toward restraint or signal flexibility. The anticipation contributed to a cautious undertone in rate-sensitive segments of the market, even as falling oil prices provided some relief to the inflation outlook.

briefs.headline: Certara Jumps as Healthcare Finds Its Footing
briefs.body: Biosimulation specialist Certara surged 8.44%, helping Healthcare post a solid 1.38% sector gain on a day when defensive and growth-adjacent medical names attracted inflows. The sector's advance contrasted with the pressure on semiconductors and energy, underscoring Monday's broader theme of capital seeking earnings visibility ahead of a week heavy with macro catalysts.
